subject: Adaptive commit proposal and split-billing mechanics for HealthCorp RFP
messages:
From: Allegra Soto <allegra.soto@healthcorp.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com; ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@proc.healthcorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthCorp RFP — clarifying commercial ask (section 5)

Evelyn / Ben —

Thanks for the initial pricing worksheet. Procurement has a follow-up for the commercial section of the RFP (section 5): HealthCorp is evaluating a multi-business-unit purchase where our three product groups (Clinical, Billing, Analytics) will each own a portion of the committed volume. We need clarity on:

- Whether Redwood supports a single enterprise commit that can be allocated to business units by HealthCorp each month (flex allocation),
- Treatment of unused commit across monthly measurement windows (carry-forward, reallocation, or forfeiture), and
- A mechanism for credits if actual usage materially drops below committed volume mid-term (rollback / downward adjustment).

Can you provide a proposed commercial mechanics section and an example calculation for a 12-month commit of 1B tokens with a 30% variable month-by-month allocation across units, plus the proposed overage token price and any discounts for up-front payment?

Appreciate a concise response we can attach to the RFP.

— Allegra
Procurement, HealthCorp
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: Allegra Soto <allegra.soto@healthcorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthCorp RFP — clarifying commercial ask (section 5)

Hi Allegra —

Thanks — we can support the model you're describing. High level summary (attached is a one-page term sheet + worked example):

1) Enterprise Adaptive Commit (EAC): single committed pool (example: 1,000,000,000 tokens for 12 months) billed monthly at an agreed committed rate. Commit can be flex-allocated by HealthCorp to business units each monthly measurement window via a simple allocation file (CSV) you upload to the console before the start of the month.

2) Unused commit handling: two options — (choose one in SOW)
   - Reallocation window (default): unused tokens from prior month roll into a 3-month reallocation buffer to be consumed by any BU. After 3 months, remaining tokens expire.
   - No carry-forward: unused tokens are forfeited (lower unit price).

3) Downward adjustment / rollback credit: if actual trailing-3-month usage drops >50% of committed run-rate, Redwood will offer a one-time rollback credit equal to 40% of the remaining unused committed tokens value (pro-rated) OR a path to renegotiate committed volume at a mutually agreed rate. Rollback can be invoked once per 12-month period.

4) Overage pricing: overage charged at 1.75x committed unit rate for the month unless a burst cushion is active. We offer an optional burst cushion (up to 15% of monthly commit) billed at 1.25x committed rate.

5) Discounts and payment terms: standard 10% volume discount for 12-month prepay; additional 5% strategic-account discount available based on customer references and case study approval.

I'll attach the worked example showing a split allocation across three BUs, monthly billing adjustment, and a sample quarterly true-up. Ben — can you review the rollback credit language and confirm we can commit to the 40% credit and single-invocation constraint? Marcus — please confirm the measurement window logic in the console will support the upload+allocation flow.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: HealthCorp RFP — clarifying commercial ask (section 5)

Eve / team —

40% rollback credit is OK from commercial — a few guardrails we should bake into the term sheet:
- Triggering condition: trailing-3-months average usage < 50% of committed monthly run-rate.
- Single invocation only.
- Credit applied as a billing credit against future invoices OR one-time refund at customer's election for enterprise prepay deals.
- For prepay deals, refunds capped at 75% of remaining prepay balance to avoid overexposure.

Also: recommend we offer a variant called "Flexible Allocation Lite" (no carry-forward, lower committed unit rate) for customers that want lower price in exchange for stricter forfeiture. We should include both options in the RFP response with worked numbers.

Ben
Head of Commercial Deals, Redwood Inference

Eve / Ben —

Console mechanics are straightforward: we already support an allocation CSV with entries: month, business_unit_id, allocated_tokens. We'll add a validation step that rejects allocations exceeding the remaining pool. Reallocation buffer (3-month) will be implemented as a ledger entry flagged as "reallocation_credit_<month>" and consumed before live capacity.

Couple of notes on billing/metrics:
- Metering window: calendar month (UTC) by default. Customer can elect vendor-month (their fiscal month) with 30-day notice.
- True-up cadence: quarterly. Monthly statements will show committed vs consumed, with auto-applied credits/charges at month end if overage triggers.
- Attribution: we can produce per-BU token breakdown and a reconciliation CSV for audits.

I'll attach a short snippet showing the expected CSV schema. Neha — for billing ops, please confirm the refund cap behavior for prepay deals.

Marcus
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Confirmed — billing team can support: 
- Refunds for prepaid contracts: cap refund to 75% of remaining prepay as Ben suggested. Remaining 25% retained to cover infrastructure spin-up costs.
- Credits: can be applied to future invoices; we will include GL mapping in SOW.
- Implementation note: if HealthCorp elects to use vendor-month different from calendar-month, there will be a one-time alignment invoice for the first partial month.

Allegra / Tom —

Thanks for the question. Please find our proposed commercial mechanics below (we will attach the one-page term sheet and a worked example spreadsheet to the formal RFP response):

Proposed commercial mechanics (summary):
- Commitment: Enterprise Adaptive Commit (EAC) — single pool of tokens for 12 months (example: 1B tokens).
- Allocation: HealthCorp can assign tokens to business units at the start of each month using the console CSV upload (month-level allocations).
- Carry-forward: Default option = 3-month reallocation buffer. Alternative option = No carry-forward (lower price). Please indicate preferred option in RFP.
- Overage: 1.75x committed unit rate. Optional burst cushion up to 15% of monthly commit at 1.25x.
- Rollback / downward adjustment: One-time rollback invoked if trailing-3-month average <50% committed run-rate; credit = 40% of remaining committed-token value (pro-rated). Refunds for prepay capped at 75% of prepay balance.
- Billing: Monthly invoices, quarterly true-up statements. Per-BU reporting and CSV audit exports provided.
- Discounts: 10% for annual prepay; +5% strategic account discount on mutual agreement.

Worked example attached: 1B tokens commit, 12 months, three BUs with 30/50/20 split in month 1 that rebalances month-to-month. The workbook shows monthly allocation, carry-forward consumption, overage calculation, and the rollback credit calculation for a hypothetical usage drop in month 8.

Next steps:
1) Allegra: confirm whether HealthCorp wants the 3-month reallocation buffer or the forfeiture (no carry-forward) option.
2) Tom: if you want the prepay scenario in the RFP, let us know the preferred billing cadence (monthly invoice vs single prepay invoice).

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the example.

Best,
Evelyn

Evelyn / team —

Thanks for the clear summary — HealthCorp prefers the 3-month reallocation buffer for flexibility. We also want the prepay example in the RFP to show the economics both ways. A couple of procurement clarifications: 

- Can you add a clause that the rollback credit is "subject to mutually agreed audit of usage logs"? We need the reconciliation trail.
- For the burst cushion, will Redwood guarantee capacity in peak months or is it best-effort? We need assurance for clinical peak windows.

If you can incorporate those two items into the term sheet, we'll include the updated language in our scoring matrix. We'll aim to include your response in the RFP submission by 2027-04-20.

Tom
Director of Procurement, HealthCorp

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-14T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthCorp RFP — clarifying commercial ask (section 5)

Tom / Allegra —

Noted and agreed. Two brief updates we'll put in the term sheet: 
1) Rollback credit will be subject to an agreed reconciliation process — HealthCorp can request the per-BU CSV exports and we will run an audit reconciliation within 10 business days; credit only applies after reconciliation sign-off.
2) Burst cushion: Redwood provides "capacity assurance" for burst cushions purchased as part of Dedicated inflight pools. For hosted/shared capacity, burst cushion is provided on a best-effort basis; we will add a service-level note that for clinical-critical windows customers should evaluate Dedicated or reserved burst add-ons.

We'll update the attached PDF and spreadsheet and push into the RFP folder. Do either of you want a quick call tomorrow morning to walk the worked example?

Thanks — Evelyn
